title: Most Gizmos do not properly render with large world coordinates despite building with Double Precision
body:
### Tested versions

4.2-4.6

### System information

Godot v4.6.beta.mono.double (a262cc3) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9159) - AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 95.14 GiB memory

### Issue description

Most gizmos will exhibit floating point issues despite using a double precision build if placed at a large world coordinate.

Gizmos should probably be rendered using a camera relative offset rather than the raw world coordinates.

Almost all gizmos with a billboard are included in this (lights, reflection probes, voxelGI, etc)

The world grid also exhibits problematic behavior.

Some gizmos render correctly, such as the selection gizmos and colliders. 

### Steps to reproduce

- Open a Godot Project with the engine built with Double Precision
- Place something that makes a gizmo billboard, like a light.
-  Move the light to something like 5,000,000 units away from origin on any axis. You may wish to also add a mesh to compare.
- Focus the editor camera on the Gizmo (F)
- Observe as the gizmo jitters but the mesh does not.
